identity.title: CO (7-6), [C I] 370 μm, and [N II] 205 μm Line Emission of the QSO BRI 1335-0417 at Redshift 4.407

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the results from our Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) imaging observations of the CO (7$-$6), [C i] 370$\,\mu{\rm m}$ (hereafter [C i]) and [N ii] 205$\,\mu{\rm m}$

evidence.quote: BRI 1335-0417, an infrared luminous QSO at $z = 4.407$ (Storrie-Lombardi et al. 1994)

evidence.quote: BRI 1335-0417, an infrared luminous QSO at $z = 4.407$ (Storrie-Lombardi et al. 1994)

question.value: What do CO(7-6), [CI] and [NII] line and continuum emission of the z=4.407 QSO BRI 1335-0417 reveal about its star formation, gas properties and merger vs disk nature?

evidence.quote: The ALMA data presented here allow for not only some quantitative characterization of the SF and gas properties, but also further testing the galaxy merger scenario for this system
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.00388.S.
The CO (7$-$6)/[C i] observation of BRI 1334-0417 was carried out in the ALMA Band 4 in the time division mode (TDM)
The separate ALMA band-6 [N ii] observation was conducted in TDM in one session on January 4, 2016

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 SPWs of 1875 MHz, 128 channels of 15.625 MHz; one SPW on the line(s), 3 for continuum; effective resolution 31.25 MHz (63 and 35 km/s)

evidence.quote: Each SPW has 128 channels with a channel width of 15.625 MHz. The effective spectral resolution is 31.25 MHz, equivalent to 63 and 35 km s$^{-1}$
CO (7$-$6) line (rest-frame 806.652 GHz or 372$\,\mu{\rm m}$)
at 370$\,\mu{\rm m}$ (809.342 GHz) of neutral carbon

A total of 40 of the 12-meter antennas were used, with baselines from 15 to 331 meters.
The observation utilized 39 of the 12-meter antennas with baselines ranging from 15 to 460 meters.
ALMA beam ($\nu_{\rm obs} \approx$ 270 GHz) | (1.1$''$$\times$0.8$''$, 64$^\circ$)

findings_qualitative.value: CO(7-6) is more compact with higher velocity dispersion than [CI] and [NII], favoring merger-triggered SF over a rotating disk

evidence.quote: a picture favoring a merger-triggered star formation (SF) scenario over an orderly rotating SF disk

findings_qualitative.value: Possible QSO-driven CO(7-6) outflow up to 500-600 km/s

evidence.quote: possible QSO-driven gas outflow that reaches a maximum line-of-sight velocity of 500 to 600 km s$^{-1}$

claims.hypothesis: Is the SF merger-driven rather than an orderly rotating disk?
claims.experiment: Compared sizes and velocity dispersion of CO(7-6), [CI], [NII]
claims.result: CO(7-6) peak dispersion ~180 km/s vs ~120 ([CI]) and ~80 ([NII]); [NII] twice as extended
claims.finding: The lines arise from different regions, favoring a merger

evidence.quote: This suggests that the three lines arise effectively from different regions, a picture that fits better with a merger-trigged SF scenario

claims.hypothesis: Is there a QSO-driven outflow in CO(7-6)?
claims.experiment: Channel maps and spectra of CO(7-6)

evidence.quote: the confirmation of this possible CO (7$-$6) gas outflow in BRI 1335-0415 still requires more sensitive observations in the future

claims.hypothesis: Does L_CO(7-6) trace SFR and T_dust agree with line ratios?
claims.experiment: Gray-body SED fit and line-ratio C(60/100)
claims.result: T_dust 41.5 K vs 41+-2 K; log L_CO/L_FIR=-4.46
